### Numerical Solution
* **Given data:**
  Voltage $V = 200\text{ V}$
  Current $I = 2\text{ A}$
  Active power $P = 200\text{ W}$
  Target power factor $\cos\phi_2 = 0.8 \text{ lagging}$

1. **Initial Power Factor ($\cos\phi_1$):**
$$P = V I \cos\phi_1 \implies 200 = 200 \times 2 \times \cos\phi_1 \implies \cos\phi_1 = 0.5$$ 
$$\phi_1 = \cos^{-1}(0.5) = 60^\circ \implies \tan\phi_1 = \tan(60^\circ) = 1.732$$

2. **Initial Reactive Power ($Q_1$):**
$$Q_1 = V I \sin\phi_1 = 200 \times 2 \times \sin(60^\circ) = 400 \times 0.866 = 346.41\text{ VAR}$$ 

3. **Final Reactive Power ($Q_2$ for $\cos\phi_2 = 0.8$):**
$$\phi_2 = \cos^{-1}(0.8) = 36.87^\circ \implies \tan\phi_2 = 0.75$$
$$Q_2 = P \tan\phi_2 = 200 \times 0.75 = 150\text{ VAR}$$ 

4. **Reactive Power of Capacitor ($Q_c$):**
$$Q_c = Q_1 - Q_2 = 346.41 - 150 = 196.41\text{ VAR}$$

5. **Capacitance ($C$):**
$$Q_c = \frac{V^2}{X_c} = V^2 \omega C \implies 196.41 = (200)^2 \times (2 \pi \times 50) \times C$$
$$196.41 = 40000 \times 314.16 \times C \implies C = \frac{196.41}{12566400} = 1.563 \times 10^{-5}\text{ F} = 15.63\,\mu\text{F}$$
proTip: Power factor improvement calculations always rely on equating the real power and finding the difference in reactive power ($Q_c = P(\tan\phi_1 - \tan\phi_2)$).
